question: A large multi-agent exploration run is paused partway through, with several agents already having completed and returned results. The architect resumes the run within the same session. What happens to the agents that had already completed?
options: A) Every agent, including the ones that already completed, is re-run from the beginning of the workflow.
B) Their cached results are reused, and only the remaining, not-yet-completed agents run live.
C) The run can only be resumed by exiting and starting an entirely new Claude Code installation on the machine.
D) All previously completed results are discarded and the run cannot be resumed at all after being paused.
correct_answers: B) Their cached results are reused, and only the remaining, not-yet-completed agents run live.
explanations: Incorrect. Re-running every agent, including completed ones, wastes the work and cost already spent and is not how a resumed run behaves within the same session.
Correct. Resuming within the same session reuses the cached results of agents that already finished and only runs the remaining agents live, avoiding redundant work.
Incorrect. Resuming happens within the existing session; exiting the session, by contrast, causes the next session to start the workflow fresh instead.
Incorrect. Completed results are not discarded on resume; the run is specifically designed to be resumable within the same session rather than starting over.
